question: Does the rule apply to the last character of the whole string or to the last character of each word, and does it only bump letters or also other characters?
expect: If only the final character is bumped: 'hello worle', 'abc deg', 'abc!', 'abc 123', 'abc xya' (z wraps to a?) or 'abc xyz' if z unchanged, 'one two thref', 'test 9', 'A B D', 'end.', 'a c'. If each word's last letter is bumped: 'hellp worle', 'abd deg', etc. Comparing these tells whether the operation is per-word or whole-string, and whether digits/punctuation/space-ending strings are left alone.

question: Does the last-character bump wrap around at the alphabet ends (z->a, Z->A), or does it stop/leave the character unchanged there?
expect: Current model predicts z->a, Z->A (wrapping). If outputs are 'a','A','quia','fiza','BUZA','topaa','A-to-A','zza','walta','jaza' then wrapping is confirmed. If z/Z stay unchanged ('z','Z','quiz','fizz','BUZZ','topaz','A-to-Z','zzz','waltz','jazz'), the rule is 'increment only if successor exists in same case', which would also explain digits/symbols unchanged. Mixed results would reveal case-specific behavior.

question: Does the rule only change the very last character of the string, or does it also change the last character when the string ends in punctuation/space followed by an earlier word boundary — i.e., is the bump applied to the final character regardless of type, and does a trailing non-letter block any change?
expect: If only the final character matters and non-letters are unchanged, all ten come back unchanged except 'helloZ' -> 'helloA'. If instead the box bumps the last letter before trailing punctuation, we'd see 'hello!'->'hellp!' etc., revealing a word-final-letter rule. This distinguishes the current whole-string-last-char model from a per-word or last-letter rule on ordinary inputs.

question: Does the bump apply only to the final character of the whole string even when the string ends in a non-letter, and is the case of the successor always matched to the original character's case (including mixed-case endings)?
expect: Current model predicts: trailing space/period blocks any change (unchanged); 'ABC def' -> 'ABC deg'; 'test 123x' -> 'test 123y'; 'Apple' -> 'ApplF'; 'zZ' -> 'aA'; 'aBcD' -> 'aBcE'; 'x y z' -> 'x y a'; 'MixedCase' -> 'MixedCasF'; 'trailing space ' unchanged.
